notes.summary: Indexed primary-source premises and retrieval evidence; the university regularization PDF was unavailable, so its original author-uploaded text was read. Imported theorems and mass laws retain separate credit.
notes.detailedSummary: Records permitted foundations P0–P5, normalization conversions, source locations and proof portions actually read. The exact retained mass manuscript was retrieved at the supplied commit. No byte identity with the unavailable regularization PDF or recursive certification of deeper source imports is claimed.
notes.text:
This note records the external premises used below, with consistent IDs. These are imported foundations, not new A–G results. There are no supplied proof notes to cite. All following mathematical arguments are ordinary unverified drafts.

P0. The assignment permits canonical psh removability across closed pluripolar sets for locally upper-bounded functions, positivity of distributional Hessians, holomorphic pullback of genuine psh functions, Poincare–Lelong, distributional Stokes, point-blowup charts, and O(E)|E=O(-1). Elementary Holder, mean-value and Cauchy estimates, polar integration, and the order of a nonzero holomorphic equation are also expressly permitted. These foundations are used only in the applications proved below. Divisor line-bundle curvature is used only for divisors; no nonclosed background is identified with line-bundle curvature.

P1. Demailly, Regularization of closed positive currents and Intersection Theory, J. Algebraic Geometry 1 (1992), 361–409, Main Theorem 1.1 and Section 2. Requested primary: https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/regularization.pdf. Shell and repeated browser requests did not retrieve that PDF. The paper's author-uploaded primary text was read at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/247379399_Regularization_of_Closed_Positive_Currents_and_Intersection_Theory; the page identifies Demailly as its uploader. This verifies the mathematical statement and relevant proof, not byte identity with the unavailable university PDF. The university publication list also identifies the exact title, journal, year and page range.

Checked passages: manuscript pp. 2–3, Main Theorem 1.1; pp. 6–12, Section 2, Proposition 2.6, Lemma 2.7, equations (2.8)–(2.14), and the final Richberg smoothing step. The source operator is D=(i/pi)partial barpartial, and its Chern curvature is c(E)=(i/(2pi))D_E^2. The main theorem takes a closed almost positive T=alpha+D psi, alpha smooth closed, and an arbitrary continuous real lower bound gamma. Gamma need not be closed. For fixed s>0 its potentials are smooth off E_s(T), and T_(s,k)>=gamma-min(lambda_k,s)u-epsilon_k omega, with continuous lambda_k decreasing to nu(T,x) and epsilon_k decreasing to zero. Section 2 proves this under c(TM)+u tensor Id>=0 in the Griffiths sense, with u smooth semipositive. Its final smoothing applies to continuous attenuated potentials off E_s(T), with arbitrarily small curvature loss. We use this permitted complete mechanism, not a general smoothing claim for singular potentials or an ordinary-type preservation theorem. In particular, the broadly worded standalone Richberg lemma is not applied to discontinuous pole-bearing potentials. Credit belongs to Demailly, Kiselman's attenuation and Richberg's smoothing.

P2. Gauduchon, Les metriques standard d'une surface complexe compacte a premier nombre de Betti pair, Asterisque 126 (1985), 129–135, Theorem 2 and its complete proof on pp. 132–133. Item: https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1985__126__129_0/. The primary PDF was read through the browser at https://numdam.org/item/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf. Theorem 2 is the general standard-metric theorem, not the separate even-Betti Theorem 1. Its real dimension 2m means complex dimension m. For complex dimension n>=2 it supplies a conformal smooth Hermitian gamma with dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0, unique up to scale. The proof reduces conformal change to a positive generator of the adjoint complex Laplacian's kernel; index zero and the maximum principle give dimension, sign and strict positivity. The source dd^c=2i partial barpartial is 4pi times the task operator, so the zero-Hessian condition is unchanged. Its conformal exponent formula is not used when n=1.

P3. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, university primary https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf, browser header version June 21, 2012. Read III.5.5–5.8, printed pp. 158–159, and III.6.8–6.9, pp. 164–165, including the growth comparison. Here D=(i/pi)partial barpartial and beta_0=(i/(2pi))partial barpartial |z|^2. For closed positive S of bidimension (p,p), r^(-2p) integral_(B(x,r)) S wedge beta_0^p is nondecreasing and tends to nu(S,x). Equivalently its Euclidean trace measure is divided by pi^p r^(2p)/p!. For genuine psh V, nu(DV,x)=lim_(r->0) sup_(sphere(x,r)) V/log r. Smooth additions and bounded differences do not change that quotient. With task operator d=dd^c=D/2, nu(dV,x) is half this function quotient; vanishing is the same. These local results do not themselves grant E's global estimate.

P4. Demailly, On the cohomology of pseudoeffective line bundles, exact arXiv:1401.5432v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.5432v2, dated January 2, 2015. Read all of Theorem 1.2 and its printed proof, pp. 6–7: every real m>0, Hilbert weight exp(-2m phi), kernel equal to the squared norm of evaluation on the unit ball, phi_m=(1/(2m))log K_m, and nu(phi)-n/m<=nu(phi_m)<=nu(phi). Its upper estimate uses mean value; its lower estimate imports Ohsawa–Takegoshi; dividing by negative log r yields the Lelong bounds. This theorem does not directly grant integrability at a zero-Lelong pole.

Also read the complete printed Section 2 chain, pp. 12–17: Theorem 2.2, Corollary 2.3, division and standard bases in 2.6–2.8, Lemma 2.9, and both parts of 2.11. Corollary 2.3 supplies local strong openness for |g|^2 exp(-2c phi). The proof chain imports Ohsawa–Takegoshi and analytic division/standard-basis foundations, which are not recursively certified here. The text extraction contains apparent slips in ancillary formulas and does not spell out subsequence extraction for almost-everywhere convergence. Those auxiliary sentences are not imported as additional premises, and this note does not certify the whole source proof. The expressly permitted established theorem and its exact weight convention are used. Set c=t/2; improved c'>c gives task exponent t'=2c'>t. No replacement or strengthened version is assumed.

P5. The assignment separately supplies the ordinary-type ruled-family mass laws and modification descent/pushforward laws. Exact retained source: https://github.com/MingchenXia/non-kahler-pluripotential-theory/blob/2ec45dec6172ced6e2af18b2b5fe657c07aeee9e/research/papers/S11-nonclosed-ruled-restricted-masses-and-strict-types.tex. It was retrieved with the GitHub file tool at that exact commit. Sections 2–5 were checked for the specified premises: every rough theta-psh representative in [r], b<c, has finite positive extended top mass; the infimum and supremum are 2(c-b)min a and 2(c-b)max a; proper smooth compact pure pullback gives a canonical full-type bijection and preserves actual extended mass under pushforward. These are separately credited established inputs. Their deeper BEGZ/background imports are not recursively certified, and the manuscript's other results are not used as proofs of A–G.

Reproducibility. Workspace: /workspace/research/native-workers/codex-51qKNr. Input: input.json. Downloader: fetch_sources.py; rerun with `python fetch_sources.py`. Runtime details and artifact hashes are recorded by `python check_artifacts.py`. No credentials, other workers or private histories were inspected, and no resource-heavy computation was launched. Source-reading evidence, analytic proofs and machine diagnostics remain distinct.

notes.summary: Proves canonical sharp extension across closed pluripolar sets, same-type divisor removal, and genuine modification pullback with continuous, possibly nonclosed lower bounds.
notes.detailedSummary: Local constant quadratic approximations recover the exact Hessian inequality after canonical removal. Both ordinary inequalities survive at every pole. Modification pullback is constructed from genuine local psh compositions and retains its lower bound across the analytic exceptional set, without restricting a singular current or factoring the modification.
notes.text:
Canonical extension, divisor removal and pullback. Write d=dd^c=(i/(2pi))partial barpartial. The proof uses the expressly permitted foundations P0 in n1.

A genuine quasi-psh a satisfies a(x)=limsup_(z->x,z outside A) a(z) for every closed locally pluripolar A. Add a smooth local function making a psh. Upper semicontinuity gives one inequality. A strict reverse inequality at a finite value would bound the psh function strictly below its value almost everywhere on a small ball, contradicting submean. Pluripolar sets have Lebesgue measure zero because their defining genuine psh functions are locally integrable. At a minus-infinity value, upper semicontinuity gives the assertion directly. Subtracting the smooth function proves the quasi-psh assertion. The same submean and upper-semicontinuity inequalities show that a genuine psh value is the limit of its ball averages. Hence genuine quasi-psh functions equal almost everywhere are equal pointwise, after adding a common local quadratic making both psh.

Let u be genuine quasi-psh off A, locally bounded above near A, with du>=eta there, eta a continuous real (1,1) form. On a relatively compact chart choose a quadratic Q with dQ>=-eta. Then u+Q is psh off A and extends canonically. Thus u extends genuinely, represented by the limsup from outside A. This extension retains du>=eta exactly. For e>0, shrink a coordinate ball about x until eta_x-e beta_0<=eta_z<=eta_x+e beta_0, viewing eta_x as constant coefficients. Choose a real quadratic L with dL=eta_x-e beta_0. The locally upper-bounded u-L is psh off A and extends psh. Its extension equals the already chosen u-L. Thus du>=eta_x-e beta_0>=eta-2e beta_0 on that ball. Such balls cover the chart for each e, so the bound holds locally everywhere. Let e tend to zero. No closedness of eta is required.

If q is genuine quasi-psh and q-C<=u<=q+C off A, taking the canonical limsups extends both inequalities at every point. In particular q(x)=-infinity forces u(x)=-infinity by the upper inequality; the lower inequality remains valid in the extended-real sense.

Divisor removal. Omit zero coefficients first. Let ell=ell_Delta, d ell=[Delta]-chi, B=theta-chi, and let w~ell+q be genuine with theta+dw>=epsilon h. Off supp Delta set u=w-ell. Since d ell=-chi there, du>=epsilon h-B. The ordinary inequalities become q-C<=u<=q+C, providing the required local upper bound. The preceding argument gives a genuine extension u~q with the retained exact inequality B+du>=epsilon h on all M. Off the divisor w=ell+u. Both sides are canonical quasi-psh functions equal almost everywhere, hence everywhere. On positive-coefficient divisor poles both sides are minus infinity. Consequently theta+dw=[Delta]+B+du globally. No restriction of w to a divisor was used. The same proof retains any continuous lower bound.

Modification pullback. Let pi:M'->M be any smooth connected compact modification. Locally write q=P-s with P genuine psh and s smooth. P composed with pi is psh and is not identically minus infinity on any open component: the isomorphism locus is dense, its image there is open, and P is finite almost everywhere. Thus q composed with pi is genuine quasi-psh, including the preimage of each pole; local constructions agree pointwise. If dq>=eta, then d(pi^*q)>=pi^*eta on the isomorphism locus. Its complement upstairs is analytic, hence locally closed pluripolar. The genuine pullback is locally upper bounded, so sharp extension gives the same bound everywhere. This proves the bound for a nonclosed eta without defining pullback of arbitrary currents. Mutual ordinary inequalities compose pointwise, including common pole values.

notes.summary: Proves E in every positive dimension: actual arbitrarily small negative curvature within one ordinary type forces zero point Lelong numbers everywhere.
notes.detailedSummary: For n>=2 a Gauduchon metric gives total positive trace mass exactly delta times a fixed constant. A local closed positive correction and normalized Lelong monotonicity yield nu(q_delta,x)<=C_x delta. Ordinary bounded difference transfers this to q. Dimension one uses total measure and its atoms.
notes.text:
Target E. Let n=dim_C M>=1. For every delta>0 take the actual genuine q_delta~q with dq_delta>=-delta h, and put T_delta=dq_delta+delta h>=0. This current is generally not closed. Closed-current monotonicity will be applied only to a different local current.

For n>=2, P2 in n1 supplies a smooth Gauduchon gamma with d gamma^(n-1)=0. Distributional Stokes is legitimate because q_delta is locally integrable and gamma is smooth on compact M. It gives
  integral_M T_delta wedge gamma^(n-1)=delta H,
  H=integral_M h wedge gamma^(n-1)>0.
No normalization, supremum or L1 bound of q_delta enters this equality of positive trace mass.

Fix arbitrary x and a relatively compact coordinate chart containing a closed ball B(x,R). Put beta_0=d|z|^2 and choose fixed A>0 with A beta_0>=h on the chart. Then
  S_delta=d(q_delta+delta A|z|^2)
         =T_delta+delta(A beta_0-h)
 is CLOSED and positive locally. Metric comparison supplies K with beta_0^(n-1)<=K gamma^(n-1) when testing positive (1,1) currents. Hence
  integral_(B(x,R)) S_delta wedge beta_0^(n-1)
  <=K delta H+delta integral_(B(x,R))(A beta_0-h) wedge beta_0^(n-1)
  <=C_x delta,
where C_x is independent of delta and q_delta. These wedges pair currents only with smooth forms.

Apply exactly P3's normalized monotonicity to S_delta, of bidimension (n-1,n-1):
  nu(S_delta,x)<=R^(-2n+2) C_x delta.
The quadratic contributes zero Lelong number. In the source function normalization this is
  nu_function(q_delta,x)<=2 R^(-2n+2) C_x delta.
Mutual ordinary bounded difference preserves the logarithmic growth quotient, so nu_function(q,x)=nu_function(q_delta,x). Nonnegativity and delta->0 prove nu(q,x)=0. The chosen point was arbitrary.

For n=1 no Gauduchon conformal exponent is used. T_delta is a positive top-degree measure and Stokes gives T_delta(M)=delta integral_M h. Its atom at x equals that of dq_delta because h is smooth. P3 with p=0 identifies this atom with the current Lelong number. Thus nu_function(q_delta,x)<=2 delta integral_M h, and ordinary-type invariance followed by delta->0 finishes the proof.

The antecedent requires actual small-curvature representatives in the same ordinary type. Regularizations changing that type do not meet it. This proves neither the converse for arbitrary zero-Lelong functions nor a theorem about their arbitrary pullbacks.

notes.summary: Proves A by regularizing the closed current dd^c q', with source potential q'/2; smoothness is global and curvature loss uniform. No same-type smoothing is asserted.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks almost positivity, the arbitrary continuous nonclosed lower bound, the tangent Chern curvature condition with u=K h, and empty Lelong superlevel sets. A fixed cutoff s=epsilon/(4K) gives a smooth f with B+dd^c f>=epsilon h/2.
notes.text:
Target A. Assume B+dq'>=epsilon h and q' is genuine quasi-psh with zero point Lelong numbers everywhere. Form the CLOSED almost positive current T=dq', not the generally nonclosed B+dq'. In P1's exact notation take alpha=0, psi=q'/2 and D=(i/pi)partial barpartial. Then T=alpha+D psi. Alpha is smooth closed, psi genuine quasi-psh, and T>=gamma with gamma=epsilon h-B smooth real, hence continuous. The primary theorem does not require gamma to be closed.

Use h as the tangent Hermitian metric. Its smooth source-normalized Chern curvature is c_h(TM)=(i/(2pi))D_TM^2. Compactness of the unit decomposable tangent tensors gives a finite lower curvature bound. Choose K>=1 large enough that
  c_h(TM)+K h tensor Id_TM>=0
in the Griffiths sense. Thus u=K h is smooth semipositive and satisfies precisely the stronger sufficient condition in the Section 2 proof. It need not be closed. Take the theorem's omega=h.

The current Lelong numbers of T=D(q'/2) are zero. Therefore E_s(T) is empty for every fixed s>0. Choose s=epsilon/(4K). P1 supplies global potentials psi_(s,k) actually smooth on M minus the empty set, hence on ALL M, with
  D psi_(s,k)>=epsilon h-B-min(lambda_k,s)K h-epsilon_k h.
The decreasing lambda_k converge to zero and are nonnegative; consequently min(lambda_k,s)K<=epsilon/4 uniformly. Choose k with epsilon_k<=epsilon/4, including the arbitrarily small loss from the source's final smoothing step. Set f=2 psi_(s,k). Since d f=D psi_(s,k),
  B+d f>=epsilon h/2
on all M. This cutoff provides a uniform curvature loss without needing a pointwise-to-uniform convergence assertion.

All curvature and normalization hypotheses are checked against P1 in n1. The mechanism is the known closed-current regularization of Demailly, with Kiselman attenuation and Richberg smoothing. Its application here uses a closed exact T with a potentially nonclosed lower bound gamma. There is no claim f~q', and regularization was never applied directly to B+dq'. In dimension zero the form inequality is vacuous and a constant suffices.

notes.summary: Proves B without an extra zero-Lelong hypothesis: a strict current in [ell_Delta+q] exists exactly when theta-chi_Delta has a smooth strictly positive gauge.
notes.detailedSummary: Necessity uses canonical divisor removal, E and A. Sufficiency uses a smooth positive gauge and an actual small-curvature same-type residual. Both ordinary inequalities are retained at logarithmic and residual poles; zero coefficients are omitted before evaluation.
notes.text:
Target B, without an extra zero-Lelong hypothesis. If M has dimension zero, connectedness makes it a point, genuine potentials are finite constants, and the form inequalities and equivalence are immediate. Assume positive dimension below.

Suppose q satisfies E's exact small-curvature same-type hypothesis. By n3 its point Lelong numbers vanish everywhere. Write ell=ell_Delta, chi=chi_Delta and B=theta-chi, omitting zero coefficients from divisor expressions and assigning their potential contribution the zero function even on the divisor.

Necessity. Suppose an actual genuine w~ell+q satisfies theta+dw>=epsilon h. Canonical divisor removal in n2 gives an actual genuine u~q with the retained sharp bound B+du>=epsilon h globally. Bounded ordinary difference preserves point Lelong numbers, so u has zero Lelong numbers. Apply n4 to B,u,epsilon. There is a smooth real f with B+d f>=epsilon h/2. This proves necessity for arbitrary smooth real theta and potentially nonclosed B.

Sufficiency. Suppose smooth f makes B+d f strictly positive. Compactness gives B+d f>=kappa h for some kappa>0. Choose an ACTUAL q_delta~q with dq_delta>=-delta h for delta<kappa/2. The genuine canonical sum
  w=ell+q_delta+f
is not identically minus infinity, and Poincare–Lelong gives
  theta+dw=[Delta]+B+d f+dq_delta
          >=[Delta]+(kappa-delta)h>=kappa h/2.
No divisor restriction occurs.

Since f is smooth bounded and q_delta~q, this is the SAME mutual ordinary type. Where ell is finite, both inequalities follow by adding ell and f to the two q_delta/q inequalities. Where ell=-infinity, both sums are minus infinity. Residual poles away from the divisor are shared by q_delta and q, hence by the sums. The zero-divisor case ell=0 introduces no undefined multiplication. These verify both bounded ordinary inequalities at every pole.

Thus a strict theta-current in the specified MUTUAL ordinary type exists if and only if B has a smooth strictly positive gauge representative. Smoothness is required of the gauge, not of the residual type. For nonclosed theta this is a statement about gauges of forms, not line-bundle curvature or a closed cohomology class.

notes.summary: Proves F for all smooth connected compact modifications under exactly E's hypothesis; canonical pullback has the same small-curvature property and zero point Lelong numbers upstairs.
notes.detailedSummary: Actual pullback representatives retain the bound -delta pi^*h, which compactness compares with any chosen h'. Ordinary inequalities compose including pole values. Applying E upstairs proves zero Lelong numbers without modification factorization or a general zero-Lelong pullback theorem.
notes.text:
Target F. Let q satisfy exactly E's hypothesis on M and let pi:M'->M be any smooth connected compact modification. Dimension is unchanged. The pointwise pullback pi^*q=q composed with pi is genuine and canonical by n2's local psh construction. No factorization and no general theorem about pullbacks of zero-Lelong functions is used.

Fix any smooth Hermitian h'>0 upstairs. Smoothness and compactness give pi^*h<=C h' for finite C>=1, even though pi^*h may be degenerate. For eta>0 choose delta=eta/C and an ACTUAL q_delta~q with dq_delta>=-delta h. By n2 its actual canonical pullback satisfies
  d(pi^*q_delta)>=-delta pi^*h>=-eta h'
EVERYWHERE on M'. Both ordinary inequalities between q_delta and q compose pointwise with pi. At preimages of poles they retain their common minus-infinity values; at finite image points they are ordinary finite inequalities. Hence pi^*q_delta~pi^*q in the genuine upstairs type.

This establishes E's antecedent on M' for every eta>0 and the chosen h'. Apply n3 ON M' to obtain zero point Lelong numbers at every point upstairs. The argument never infers a theorem for arbitrary pullbacks of arbitrary zero-Lelong functions: its essential input is the stronger actual same-type small-curvature hypothesis.

notes.summary: Proves C using explicit shifted residuals U_L=L^alpha-(L-G_p)^alpha, with genuine same-type small-curvature representatives and zero Lelong numbers at every infinitely near point.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the global bounded-difference inequalities and curvature loss alpha L^(alpha-1). A two-chart induction yields finite monomial multiplicities at every point after arbitrary finite point-blowup stages. Spherical supremum growth is sublogarithmic at all such points.
notes.text:
Target C. Pull G=G_p from the first P1 to Y=P1 x P1, retaining genuine pole values. For L>=1 define
  U_L=L^alpha-(L-G)^alpha,
with U_L=-infinity wherever G=-infinity. Then U_1=U and max U_L=0. For t=-G>=0, concavity, or integration of alpha(s+t)^(alpha-1) from s=1 to L, gives
  0<=(L+t)^alpha-(1+t)^alpha<=L^alpha-1.
Therefore
  U<=U_L<=U+(L^alpha-1)
at finite points; at poles both functions have their actual minus-infinity values. Thus U_L~U genuinely.

For F_L(x)=L^alpha-(L-x)^alpha on x<=0,
  0<F_L'(x)=alpha(L-x)^(alpha-1)<=eta_L=alpha L^(alpha-1),
  F_L''(x)=alpha(1-alpha)(L-x)^(alpha-2)>0.
Off D, dG=-w1. The chain rule gives
  dF_L(G)=F_L'(G)dG+F_L''(G)(i/(2pi))partial G wedge barpartial G
         >=-eta_L w1.
The functions are locally upper bounded. Adding a smooth local quadratic and applying canonical extension as in n2 produces genuine quasi-psh functions across D retaining this exact bound. Their explicit limiting pole value is minus infinity. Consequently dU_L>=-eta_L w1 globally and eta_L->0.

For any finite composition pi:Y'->Y of point blowups, n2 gives actual canonical pullbacks U_L composed with pi, sharing all poles and retaining both ordinary inequalities, with
  d(pi^*U_L)>=-eta_L pi^*w1.
Given any fixed h'>0 upstairs, compactness gives pi^*w1<=K h' for finite K>=1. Choosing L so K eta_L<delta proves the actual same-type small-curvature assertion.

Every point Lelong number is also checked directly. On the base near p,
  G=log|z1|^2+smooth,
by the local Fubini–Study potential and Poincare–Lelong, or the explicit normalized Green function log(|z1|^2/(1+|z1|^2)) after putting p=0. Under point blowups the total transform of D remains locally a normal-crossing monomial. At an arbitrary center with equation z1^m1 z2^m2 times a unit, the two blowup charts give
  x^(m1+m2)y^m2 times a unit,
  x^m1 y^(m1+m2) times a unit.
Absent components mean exponent zero. Outside the total transform both exponents are zero; on one component only its exponent contributes; at a crossing the new exceptional multiplicity is the sum. Inductively, at EVERY point of every finite stage,
  pi^*G=log|z1^m1 z2^m2|^2+sigma,
with finite nonnegative integer exponents and sigma smooth, and at most two positive exponents.

When m1+m2>0, on each sufficiently small coordinate sphere of radius r choose a direction with relevant coordinates comparable to r and nonzero. Then pi^*G=2(m1+m2)log r+O(1) in that direction. Since pi^*U<=0,
  -C(1+|log r|)^alpha<=sup_(sphere(r)) pi^*U<=0.
Adding a smooth local function making the pullback psh changes the supremum by a bounded amount. Dividing by negative log r gives a quotient tending to zero because alpha<1. P3's spherical growth formula proves zero point Lelong number. If both exponents vanish, the function is smooth and the conclusion is immediate. This checks every infinitely near point without assuming a general zero-Lelong pullback theorem.

notes.summary: Proves D for every nonempty finite point-blowup composition and all pole centers: mutual-type strict currents are impossible, actual recursive one-sided strict witnesses exist, and supplied full-type mass extrema persist.
notes.detailedSummary: B reduces the obstruction to a smooth positive residual gauge, whose restriction to the last exceptional P1 contradicts Stokes. Each blowup adds an exceptional logarithm whose curvature repairs the collapsed direction with a global Hermitian margin. The witness changes ordinary type. The imported competitor bijection and mass pushforward apply only to the original full pulled-back type.
notes.text:
Target D. Put k=c-b>0, beta=k w1+a w2, theta=c w1+a w2 and r=bG+U. The declared type is nonempty: n7 supplies U_L~U with eta_L<k, and
  theta+d(bG+U_L)>=b[D]+(k-eta_L)w1+a w2,
which is strict relative to w1+w2. The reference r itself need not already be theta-psh; it specifies the type.

Exclusion after every NONEMPTY composition. For pi:Y'->Y let Delta'=b pi^*D, ell'=b pi^*G and chi'=b pi^*w1. If b=0 these are the zero divisor, function and curvature, including on poles. The residual q'=pi^*U has the actual small-curvature same-type property by n7. Apply n5 to pi^*theta. Any hypothetical strict current with genuine potential w'~pi^*r would force a SMOOTH f with
  pi^*beta+d f>=epsilon h'
for some epsilon>0 and positive Hermitian h'. Let E be the exceptional curve of the LAST blowup. On the final surface it is a smooth P1 and the entire pi maps it to one point of Y, irrespective of earlier centers. Thus the restriction of the smooth pi^*beta to E is zero. Restricting only the smooth f and integrating gives
  0=integral_E d(f|E)>=epsilon integral_E h'>0,
a contradiction. This works even when the original potentials are identically minus infinity on E. No singular current was restricted.

Actual recursive one-sided witness. Write pi as mu_j:Y_j->Y_(j-1), j=1,...,m. Start with v_0=bG+U_L above, so theta_0+dv_0>=epsilon_0 h_0 for some smooth Hermitian h_0 and epsilon_0>0. Suppose theta_(j-1)+dv_(j-1)>=epsilon_(j-1)h_(j-1), and set theta_j=mu_j^*theta_(j-1).

Choose a smooth metric on O(E_j) whose curvature chi_j restricts to negative probability Fubini–Study curvature on E_j. This is possible because O(E_j)|E_j=O_P1(-1): prescribe its standard metric there, compare with a global smooth metric, and extend the smooth logarithm of their positive ratio using local tubular charts and a partition of unity. Poincare–Lelong gives a genuine ell_j with d ell_j=[E_j]-chi_j. Normalize ell_j<=0 by adding a constant.

Set A=epsilon_(j-1)mu_j^*h_(j-1) and C=-chi_j. The smooth A is semipositive, positive off E_j, and its kernel on E_j is precisely the tangent line to E_j. C is positive on that kernel. A uniform small t_j>0 makes A+t_j C strictly positive on ALL Y_j. To prove uniformity, use any smooth unit tangent bundle. The compact zero locus of A on unit vectors lies over E_j; C has a positive minimum there and stays positive on a neighborhood. On the compact complement A has a positive minimum a_0, while C>=-C_0 everywhere. Choosing 0<t_j<a_0/(C_0+1) gives positivity on both sets. Compactness supplies an actual quantitative Hermitian lower bound.

By n2's sharp pullback inequality, the actual genuine potential

satisfies

Shrink so phi<=A for a finite constant A on Omega. Its point Lelong number at x is zero. Set m=s/2>0. Use precisely P4's Hilbert space H with norm squared integral_Omega |g|^2 exp(-2m phi), kernel K_m(z)=sup_(norm g<=1)|g(z)|^2, and genuine psh phi_m=(1/(2m))log K_m. The theorem gives nu(phi_m,x)<=nu(phi,x)=0.

Suppose every g in H vanishes at x. A weighted unit vector has unweighted L2 norm squared at most exp(2mA). Mean-value and Cauchy estimates give a uniform first derivative bound on a smaller ball. Thus |g(z)|<=C|z-x| there, uniformly on the weighted unit ball. Taking its supremum gives K_m(z)<=C^2|z-x|^2 and
  phi_m(z)<=(1/m)log|z-x|+O(1).
The growth formula implies nu(phi_m,x)>=1/m>0, a contradiction. H={0} is likewise excluded by Theorem 1.2, which supplies a nonidentically-minus-infinity Bergman potential and its zero upper Lelong bound. Some g in H therefore has g(x)!=0. On a smaller neighborhood |g|>=d_0>0, so
  integral exp(-s phi)<=d_0^(-2) integral |g|^2 exp(-2m phi)<infinity.
The bounded smooth sigma converts this to integrability of exp(-s q). Since x and s were arbitrary, this holds locally everywhere for EVERY s>0. Smooth positive dV is locally comparable to Lebesgue measure. No Skoda integrability theorem or finite-generation statement about the kernel was imported.

Ambient neutrality. Let v be ANY genuine quasi-psh function and t>0. Since q is locally bounded above, integrability of |g|^2 exp(-t(v+q)) implies integrability of |g|^2 exp(-tv). Hence I(t(v+q)) is contained in I(tv).

Conversely, take g in I(tv). Add bounded smooth sigma_v making v+sigma_v psh, and apply P4's EXACT strong openness with c=t/2. After shrinking there is t'=2c'>t with integral |g|^2 exp(-t'v)<infinity. Put p=t'/t>1 and p'=p/(p-1). The holomorphic g is bounded on a still smaller ball, so
  integral (|g|^2 exp(-tv))^p
  =integral |g|^(2p) exp(-t'v)<infinity,
since |g|^(2p)<=C|g|^2. The first part gives integral exp(-t p' q)<infinity. Holder now yields
  integral |g|^2 exp(-t(v+q))
  <=(integral |g|^(2p) exp(-t'v))^(1/p)
    (integral exp(-t p' q))^(1/p')<infinity.
Shrinking may depend on the germ and exponent, exactly as ideal membership permits. Therefore I(t(v+q))=I(tv) for every real t>0. Exact SNC intrinsic traces. Omit zero coefficients BEFORE restricting any equation. Use the usual distinct components of an SNC divisor, combining repetitions first. Locally

where the positive components through the point are coordinate hyperplanes. A transverse order l>=0 in one variable gives radial integral integral_0^epsilon r^(2l-2t a_j+1)dr. It converges exactly when l>t a_j-1; the smallest nonnegative integer is floor(t a_j). At an integer endpoint t a_j=N, l=N-1 has exponent -1 and diverges, while l=N converges. This includes all integer endpoints and t a_j<1.

Consequently
  I(t ell_Delta)=O_M(-sum_(a_j>0)floor(t a_j)D_j).
For multivariable necessity, take a germ's lowest transverse power in each z_j. Its nonzero leading coefficient is nonzero on an open set of the other variables away from their divisors; Fubini and the one-variable integral force the stated divisibility. Divisibility by each coordinate power means divisibility by their product, by convergent power series. Conversely the quotient is holomorphic bounded on a smaller polydisc, and Fubini with the strict polar inequalities proves integrability. The smooth term has no effect. Ambient neutrality gives the identical formula for I(t(ell_Delta+q)).

Let Y be smooth connected compact and contained in none of the positive-coefficient D_j. Dividing by t,

Thus, for real t->infinity, the finite original intrinsic trace is EXACTLY

All prime divisors on all smooth compact modifications are covered without factorization. For dimension-zero Y there are no prime divisors upstairs, so the last assertion is vacuous.
